(Así adicionado el inciso anterior por el artículo 1° del decreto ejecutivo N° 43932 del 25 de enero de 2023)

answers.implementation_then_now: In both periods the DGME processes the family-link categories routinely, with long delays and strict documentary demands but no documented systematic denial. Before 2023: the Defensoría (reported by La República, Sept. 2021) found 7,762 regularisation applications pending, some dating from 2019. 2023-2026: Tico Times (Oct. 2025) reports 38,000 pending applications and decision times of 12-20 months. In Nov. 2024 the Sala Constitucional condemned the DGME for 4-5 month delays on children's dependant-residence applications, which the DGME then rejected on documentary grounds (Semanario Universidad, Dec. 2024). Delays grew, but the rights are still granted in the main, so 'Usually' holds on both dates.

answers.sourcing_note: SINALEVI's consolidated text was read with its per-article amendment notes. The last notes on Ley 8764 arts. 78-79 date from Ley 9710 (2019). On Reglamento arts. 137, 138 and 203, the only notes date from Decree 38844 (2015), Decree 42389 (2022) and Decree 43932 (2023, non-family subsection). No family-relevant amendment falls in the window. Practice evidence is from the press, not from DGME statistics broken down by family category.

answers.implementation_then_now: Both before and after 2023 the Sala Constitucional hears amparo claims against the DGME on residence and family matters and rules against it. The Nov. 2024 ruling on children's dependant-residence delays (Semanario Universidad, Dec. 2024) shows the remedy working in the window. It also shows its limits: the DGME complied by deciding, then rejected the applications. Pre-2023 practice rests on the 2009 ruling (Voto 2009-01024) and on Defensoría findings on delays (2021). No shift in access to the courts is documented, so 'Usually' holds on both dates.

practice_sources.title: Migración negó estatus de residentes a niños que le ganaron recurso de amparo (Semanario Universidad)
Defensoría de los Habitantes: Migración tiene pendiente de resolver más de 7 mil solicitudes de regularización (La República)

answers.sourcing_note: The amendment notes on Ley 8764 arts. 25, 29 and 225 show no change in the window (the only 2024 amendment, Ley 10493, touched arts. 33, 241 and 253). The Constitution arts. 41/48/49 and the Código Procesal Contencioso-Administrativo were not re-read in this pass, and no constitutional amendment to those articles in 2023-2025 is known. Voto 2009-01024 was not re-opened.

provisions.instrument: Decreto Ejecutivo N.º 41329-MGP, Reglamento para el Reconocimiento de Derechos Migratorios a Parejas del Mismo Sexo
Ley General de Migración y Extranjería N.º 8764

answers.implementation_then_now: Same-sex marriage has been legal since May 2020, and same-sex spouses use the ordinary gender-neutral spousal routes. The first recognition under Decree 41329 dates from 2019 (El Mundo CR). No report of refusals or of a policy change in 2023-2025 was found, so 'Usually' is kept on both dates. Practice evidence for either period is thin and mostly pre-2023.
answers.sourcing_note: Arts. 137(b) of the Reglamento and 73 of Ley 8764 were read in SINALEVI with their amendment notes, and neither changed in the window. Decree 41329-MGP could not be located in SINALEVI, and searches returned only secondary sources, so its status is not established. The equal-marriage ruling and its 2020 entry into force predate the window.
answers.starting_answer_concern: The 'Yes' rests mainly on Decree 41329, whose official text and current status were not verified, and on the gender-neutral 'cónyuge' wording after marriage equality. The answer looks right, but its sourcing is weak.
answers.notes: No practice source was opened in this session for either period; the starting answer's evidence (El Mundo CR 2019) predates both dates.

answers.change_2023_2026: There have been no right protections neither in 2023 nor in 2026

events.what_changed: Repealed the Reglamento's provisions on investors and their dependants; that category moved to the Ley 9996 regulation, which keeps investment thresholds. The dependants route therefore stays tied to the principal's financial requirements. Arts. 31, 100 and 137, which carry the No, were untouched, so the answer does not change.

events.instrument: Ley N° 10493 del 5 de junio del 2024
events.what_changed: Extended the fee exemptions to cross-border indigenous persons and cut fees by up to 50% for seasonal agricultural workers. It does not touch family-reunification resource conditions (CCSS insurance, economic dependence).
events.passage: En el caso de trabajadores del sector agrícola, que atienden labores de cosecha temporales por periodos de nueve meses o inferiores, el costo de estos pagos será de hasta un cincuenta por ciento (50%) menos. (Así reformado el párrafo anterior por el artículo 1° de la ley N° 10493 del 5 de junio del 2024)

answers.implementation_then_now: The protection answer is the lowest option on both dates, so implementation does not apply. The CCSS-insurance and economic-dependence conditions stayed in force throughout the window.
answers.sourcing_note: SINALEVI's amendment notes show art. 31 with no amendment note. Art. 100's last note is from Decree 42389 (2022), art. 203's last note is from Decree 42389 (2022), and Ley 8764 art. 78's last note is from Ley 9710 (2019), so all predate the window. The article number of the 'Dependiente' definition was still not seen.
answers.notes: The exact entry-into-force dates of Decree 43926 (dated 14 Feb. 2023) and Ley 10493 (dated 5 June 2024) were not read; both fall after 1 Jan. 2023 and before 1 Jan. 2026, and neither changes the answer.
